title: The Window Plant
moral: Responsibility means caring for what is trusted to us. If we make a mistake, we should admit it and work to make things right.

pages.text:
Mariam's grandmother kept a small plant on the kitchen window.

It had round green leaves and one tiny white flower.

"Water it every morning," Grandma said before leaving for three days. "Only a little."

Mariam nodded. "I will take care of it."

The first morning, she watered it.

The second morning, she forgot.

She remembered at night and quickly poured water into the pot.

On the third morning, she forgot again because her cousin had come over with a puzzle book.

The puzzle had a picture of a fish wearing glasses.

"That fish looks like our maths teacher," her cousin said.

Mariam laughed so much she forgot the plant completely.

When Grandma returned, the plant looked tired. The leaves were drooping. The flower had fallen onto the soil.

Mariam's heart sank.

Grandma touched the leaves gently.

"I forgot," Mariam said. "I am sorry."

Grandma did not shout.

"This plant was trusted to you," she said softly. "Trust is not only for big things."

Mariam felt worse than if Grandma had scolded her.

"Can we save it?" she asked.

"We can try," Grandma said.

For the next week, Mariam cared for the plant carefully.

She gave it a little water each morning. She moved it where sunlight touched the window. She even told her cousin, "No fish puzzles before plant duty."

Her cousin nodded. "Very strict gardener."

Day by day, the leaves lifted.

One morning, Mariam saw a new white bud.

"Grandma!" she called.

Grandma came and smiled.

The bud was small, but to Mariam it looked like a gift.

She touched the pot carefully.

"I nearly lost it," she whispered.

Grandma placed a hand on her shoulder.

"And then you learned to care for it."

Mariam looked at the little bud glowing in the morning light.

It was not just a flower. It was a second chance.
